name: Risk Department
description: Organisational department responsible for credit risk assessment and management, including mortgage underwriting guidance and risk appetite oversight. Listed as owner and responsible party for this credit risk assessment guide.

name: Lending Department
description: Organisational department responsible for mortgage lending operations and underwriting execution. Shares ownership of the credit risk assessment guide with the Risk department.
context: Audience | Mortgage Underwriters, Risk Analysts, Lending Team

name: Mortgage Product
description: Residential mortgage lending product subject to credit risk assessment and underwriting controls. This guide provides the framework for mortgage underwriting at FirstUK Bank.
context: FirstUK Bank — Credit Risk Assessment Guide (Mortgage Underwriting)
Audience | Mortgage Underwriters, Risk Analysts, Lending Team

name: Mortgage Underwriter
description: Bank staff responsible for executing mortgage credit risk assessment and underwriting decisions in accordance with this guide. Primary audience for the credit risk assessment framework.
context: Audience | Mortgage Underwriters, Risk Analysts, Lending Team

name: Risk Analyst
description: Bank staff responsible for analysing credit risk and supporting underwriting decisions. Audience for the credit risk assessment guide.
context: Audience | Mortgage Underwriters, Risk Analysts, Lending Team

name: Head of Risk
description: Senior leadership role responsible for ownership and governance of the credit risk assessment guide. Accountable for risk framework oversight and policy maintenance.

name: Credit Risk
description: Credit risk associated with residential mortgage lending, managed within FirstUK Bank's defined risk appetite of less than 0.5% loss ratio. This risk category governs the assessment and approval of mortgage applications to ensure consistent lending decisions.
context: Provide standardized procedures for assessing credit risk on residential mortgage applications
ensuring consistent lending decisions aligned with FirstUK Bank's risk appetite (<0.5% loss ratio)

name: Mortgage Loss Ratio
description: Quantitative risk appetite threshold for residential mortgage portfolio, expressed as a maximum acceptable loss ratio. FirstUK Bank's stated appetite is less than 0.5%.
context: FirstUK Bank's risk appetite (<0.5% loss ratio)

name: Mortgage Credit Risk
description: FirstUK Bank's defined credit risk category for mortgage portfolios, with stated appetite thresholds for loss ratios, default rates, and borrower leverage constraints. The risk framework establishes maximum acceptable loss at 0.5% annually and default rate tolerance at <2% of active mortgages.
context: FirstUK Bank Mortgage Credit Risk Target
Maximum Loss Ratio: 0.5% annually (max £2.5k loss per £500k portfolio)
Default Rate Target: <2% (max 2% of active mortgages in default at any time)
LTV Limit: Max 95% (no negative equity scenarios)

name: Maximum Loss Ratio
description: Quantitative risk appetite threshold for FirstUK Bank's mortgage portfolio, expressed as a maximum annual loss ratio of 0.5%, equivalent to £2.5k loss per £500k portfolio.
context: Maximum Loss Ratio: 0.5% annually (max £2.5k loss per £500k portfolio)

name: Default Rate Target
description: Key risk indicator for mortgage portfolio health, with a target threshold of <2%, representing the maximum acceptable proportion of active mortgages in default at any time.
context: Default Rate Target: <2% (max 2% of active mortgages in default at any time)

name: Loan-to-Value Limit
description: Maximum loan-to-value ratio constraint of 95% applied to mortgage origination, designed to prevent negative equity scenarios and protect against property value depreciation.
context: LTV Limit: Max 95% (no negative equity scenarios)

name: Debt-to-Income Limit
description: Maximum debt-to-income ratio of 45% applied as a borrower income constraint during mortgage underwriting, to ensure borrower repayment capacity.

name: Mortgage
description: FirstUK Bank's mortgage product subject to defined credit risk appetite, loss ratio targets, default rate thresholds, and borrower leverage constraints outlined in the credit risk framework.
context: FirstUK Bank Mortgage Credit Risk Target

name: Loss Ratio
description: A quantitative risk indicator measuring credit losses as a percentage of portfolio value. The target threshold is set at less than 0.5%, with actual Q4 2025 performance at 0.23%, indicating performance well within risk appetite.

name: Default Rate
description: A key risk indicator tracking the percentage of accounts in default status. The target threshold is less than 2%, with actual Q4 2025 performance at 1.2%, demonstrating strong credit quality within risk appetite.

name: Average Loan-to-Value Ratio
description: A risk metric measuring the average loan-to-value ratio across the mortgage or secured lending portfolio. The target threshold is less than 80%, with actual Q4 2025 performance at 72%, indicating conservative lending practices.

name: Debt-to-Income Ratio
description: A risk metric measuring the average debt-to-income ratio of borrowers in the portfolio. The target threshold is less than 45%, with actual Q4 2025 performance at 38%, reflecting conservative underwriting standards.

name: Mortgage Product
description: A mortgage lending product subject to underwriting assessment. The document outlines the application assessment process for mortgage products, including evaluation of borrower information, property details, and loan terms.

name: Borrower
description: A natural person applying for a mortgage product. The underwriting process captures borrower information including personal details, employment, income, credit history, assets, and liabilities for assessment.

name: Mortgage Account
description: A mortgage account established following underwriting assessment. The account is defined by loan term, rate type (fixed or variable), and property collateral.

name: Credit Risk
description: Credit risk associated with mortgage lending, assessed through borrower credit history, CIBIL score, past defaults, income stability, and existing liabilities. This risk is evaluated as part of the mortgage application assessment process.

name: Property Valuation Risk
description: Risk related to the adequacy and stability of property collateral securing the mortgage. Assessment includes professional property valuation, property type, location, and area risk assessment.

name: Payment History Risk
description: Credit risk factor assessing borrower payment behaviour, weighted at 35% in the automated credit scoring model. Ranges from no missed payments (excellent) to regular late payments (poor), directly influencing credit score and lending decision.
context: Payment History | 35% | No missed payments (excellent) → Regular late payments (poor)

name: Credit Utilization Risk
description: Credit risk factor measuring the proportion of available credit used by the borrower, weighted at 20% in the scoring model. Low card balances indicate good credit management, while high balances signal elevated risk.
context: Credit Utilization | 20% | Low balance on cards (good) → High balance (poor)

name: Credit Age Risk
description: Credit risk factor reflecting the length of the borrower's credit history, weighted at 15% in the scoring model. Longer credit history demonstrates established creditworthiness, while new credit only indicates higher risk.
context: Credit Age | 15% | Longer credit history (good) → New credit only (poor)

name: Credit Inquiry Risk
description: Credit risk factor assessing the frequency of recent credit inquiries, weighted at 10% in the scoring model. Few recent inquiries indicate stable credit-seeking behaviour, while many recent inquiries suggest financial distress or over-leveraging.
context: Credit Inquiries | 10% | Few recent inquiries (good) → Many recent inquiries (poor)

name: Default and Delinquency Risk
description: Credit risk factor measuring the borrower's history of defaults or delinquencies, weighted at 20% in the automated credit scoring model. No defaults indicate excellent credit standing, while recent defaults signal very high risk.

name: Automated Credit Score
description: Quantitative credit scoring metric on a 0–100 scale used to assess borrower creditworthiness and determine lending decisions. Score ranges from Very Poor (<60) to Excellent (90–100), with corresponding risk ratings and automated or manual underwriting actions.
context: 90–100 | Excellent | Very Low | Auto-Approve (if other criteria met)

name: Excellent Credit Score Threshold
description: Credit score range indicating excellent creditworthiness with very low risk, triggering automatic approval if other lending criteria are met. Represents the bank's appetite for lowest-risk borrowers.
context: 90–100 | Excellent | Very Low | Auto-Approve (if other criteria met)

name: Good Credit Score Threshold
description: Credit score range indicating good creditworthiness with low risk, requiring standard underwriting procedures. Represents the bank's appetite for low-risk borrowers with routine review.

name: Fair Credit Score Threshold
description: Credit score range indicating fair creditworthiness with medium risk, requiring enhanced review procedures. Represents the bank's tolerance for medium-risk borrowers with additional scrutiny.

name: Poor Credit Score Threshold
description: Credit score range indicating poor creditworthiness with high risk, requiring manager review and potential decline. Represents the bank's lower tolerance for high-risk borrowers.

name: Very Poor Credit Score Threshold
description: Credit score range indicating very poor creditworthiness with very high risk, resulting in automatic decline. Represents the bank's minimum acceptable credit quality threshold.

name: Mortgage Product
description: A mortgage lending product subject to income qualification and verification procedures. The document establishes underwriting criteria for primary and secondary income assessment, including employment history verification, income stability evaluation, and conservative qualification factors applied to different employment and income types.
context: Primary Income (Employment): Verify with employer (letter on company letterhead)

name: Income Verification Process
description: A Know Your Customer control requiring verification of applicant income through employer letters, employment history checks, and assessment of income stability. The process applies differentiated qualification factors based on employment type and income source to calculate conservative qualifying income.
context: Verify with employer (letter on company letterhead)
Assess income stability (stable job vs. new employment)

name: Mortgage Applicant
description: A prospective customer applying for a mortgage product, subject to income verification and qualification procedures. The applicant's income is assessed across primary employment and secondary income sources using defined qualification factors.
context: Spouse income: Only if married/civil partnership

name: Employer
description: The applicant's employer, whose verification is required as part of income assessment. Employment letters on company letterhead are used to confirm employment status, tenure, and income.
context: Verify with employer (letter on company letterhead)

name: Employment Stability Risk
description: A credit risk factor reflecting the applicant's employment tenure and type. The risk is mitigated through differentiated qualification factors: permanent employment of 2+ years qualifies at 100%, while permanent employment under 2 years qualifies at 75%, and self-employment under 2 years is not acceptable.
context: Assess income stability (stable job vs. new employment)

name: Secondary Income Volatility Risk
description: A credit risk reflecting the variability and sustainability of secondary income sources. The risk is managed through conservative qualification factors: bonus and commission income qualifies at 50% of average, rental income at 75% to account for vacancy, and dividend/pension income at 100% if sustainable and stable.

name: Income Documentation Risk
description: A compliance risk related to the authenticity and sufficiency of income documentation. The risk is controlled through requirements for employer letters on company letterhead and minimum 2-year employment history verification.
context: Verify with employer (letter on company letterhead)

name: Spouse Income Dependency Risk
description: A credit risk arising from reliance on spouse income in qualifying income calculations. The risk is controlled by limiting spouse income qualification to documented married or civil partnership status only.
context: Spouse income: Only if married/civil partnership

name: Permanent Employment Qualification Factor
description: A qualification factor applied to primary income from permanent employment of 2 or more years. This metric represents the bank's appetite to accept full stated salary as qualifying income for stable, long-tenure employment.

name: New Permanent Employment Qualification Factor
description: A qualification factor applied to primary income from permanent employment of less than 2 years. This metric reflects reduced appetite for income stability in newer employment, qualifying at 75% of stated salary.

name: Contract Employment Qualification Factor
description: A qualification factor applied to primary income from contract employment with more than 1 year remaining. This metric qualifies contract income at 75% of stated salary, reflecting uncertainty in contract renewal.
context: Contract, >1 year remaining: 75% of stated salary

name: Self-Employed Income Qualification Factor
description: A qualification factor applied to primary income from self-employment of 2 or more years. This metric qualifies self-employed income at 75% of average last 2 years, reflecting income volatility and documentation complexity.
context: Self-employed, 2+ years: 75% of average last 2 years

name: Bonus and Commission Qualification Factor
description: A qualification factor applied to bonus and commission income. This metric qualifies such income at 50% of average last 2 years, reflecting significant volatility and discretionary nature.

name: Rental Income Qualification Factor
description: A qualification factor applied to secondary rental income. This metric qualifies rental income at 75%, with the 25% reduction accounting for potential vacancy periods and maintenance costs.

name: Dividend Income Qualification Factor
description: A qualification factor applied to secondary dividend income when sustainable and supported by 2+ years history. This metric qualifies dividend income at 100%, reflecting confidence in sustained investment returns.

name: Pension and Benefits Qualification Factor
description: A qualification factor applied to secondary pension and benefits income when guaranteed and stable. This metric qualifies such income at 100%, reflecting the certainty of government-backed or contractually guaranteed payments.

name: Mortgage Product
description: A residential mortgage product with a principal amount of £300,000, offered at 4.5% interest rate over a 25-year term. The product is subject to debt assessment and affordability evaluation as part of the lending decision process.

name: Car Loan
description: A car financing product included in the debt assessment calculation. Monthly payments are factored into the applicant's total debt obligations.

name: Credit Card Product
description: A credit card product included in debt assessment. Outstanding balances are calculated at 5% of the balance or the minimum payment, whichever is higher, for affordability purposes.
context: Credit Cards | Yes (5% of balance, or minimum payment, whichever higher)

name: Student Loan
description: A student financing product included in the debt assessment. Actual monthly payments are included in the total debt obligations calculation.

name: Debt-to-Income Ratio
description: A key affordability metric calculated as total monthly debt obligations (including proposed mortgage) divided by gross monthly income. Used to assess lending risk and borrower capacity to service debt.
context: Debt-to-Income Ratio = (Monthly Debt + Mortgage) / Monthly Income

name: Proposed Mortgage Payment Calculation
description: The calculated monthly mortgage payment obligation of £1,519 derived from a £300,000 principal at 4.5% interest over 300 months. This payment is included in the debt-to-income ratio assessment.

name: Loan-to-Value Ratio Risk
description: Credit risk assessment based on the ratio of mortgage amount to property value. FirstUK Bank applies differentiated LTV limits by credit grade, with risk escalating from low risk at ≤70% LTV to very high risk at >95% LTV. Higher LTV ratios indicate reduced equity buffers and increased default probability.
context: FirstUK Bank LTV Limits by Credit Grade

name: LTV Ratio Threshold - Excellent Credit Grade
description: Maximum LTV threshold for customers with excellent credit grade (90+). FirstUK Bank permits up to 95% LTV for this segment at standard pricing with no rate premium applied.
context: Credit Grade | Max LTV | Pricing Impact

name: LTV Ratio Threshold - Good Credit Grade
description: Maximum LTV threshold for customers with good credit grade (80–89). FirstUK Bank permits up to 90% LTV for this segment with a +0.25% rate premium applied to pricing.
context: Credit Grade | Max LTV | Pricing Impact

name: LTV Ratio Threshold - Fair Credit Grade
description: Maximum LTV threshold for customers with fair credit grade (70–79). FirstUK Bank permits up to 85% LTV for this segment with a +0.50% rate premium applied to pricing.
context: Credit Grade | Max LTV | Pricing Impact

name: LTV Ratio Threshold - Poor Credit Grade
description: Maximum LTV threshold for customers with poor credit grade (60–69). FirstUK Bank permits up to 80% LTV for this segment; applications may be declined at higher LTV ratios.
context: Credit Grade | Max LTV | Pricing Impact

name: LTV Ratio Threshold - Very Poor Credit Grade
description: Lending policy for customers with very poor credit grade (<60). FirstUK Bank does not offer mortgage lending to this segment; all applications are declined regardless of LTV.
context: Credit Grade | Max LTV | Pricing Impact

name: Mortgage Product
description: FirstUK Bank's mortgage lending product subject to LTV-based credit risk assessment and pricing differentiation by credit grade. The product applies tiered LTV limits and rate premiums based on borrower credit quality and equity position.
context: FirstUK Bank LTV Limits by Credit Grade

name: Property Location Risk
description: Risk assessment factor evaluating property location stability and market conditions. Ranges from prime areas with stable values (low risk) through growing suburban areas (medium risk) to declining areas (high risk). Location directly impacts property value sustainability and collateral quality.
context: Location | Prime area, stable values | Growing suburban | Declining area

name: Property Type Risk
description: Risk assessment factor evaluating the property type and construction characteristics. Standard property types (houses, flats) present low risk, newer construction presents medium risk, and unusual properties such as listed buildings present high risk due to valuation and marketability challenges.
context: Property Type | House, flat | Newer construction | Listed building, unusual

name: Property Condition Risk
description: Risk assessment factor evaluating the physical condition and state of repair of the property. Modern properties in good repair present low risk, average condition properties present medium risk, and properties requiring significant repairs present high risk to collateral value.
context: Condition | Modern, good repair | Average condition | Poor, repairs needed

name: Market Liquidity Risk
description: Risk assessment factor evaluating the ease and speed with which a property can be sold in the market. Properties easy to sell with active buyer interest present low risk, moderate sales activity presents medium risk, and properties hard to sell with few buyers present high risk to recovery in default scenarios.
context: Market Liquidity | Easy to sell, buyers | Moderate sales | Hard to sell, few buyers

name: Loan-to-Value Ratio Risk
description: Risk arising when property valuation falls below purchase price, triggering higher LTV and increased credit exposure. May require renegotiation, additional deposit, or borrower shortfall contribution to maintain acceptable risk parameters.
context: May require renegotiation or additional deposit

name: Loan-to-Value Ratio
description: Key risk metric used to assess mortgage lending risk by comparing loan amount to property valuation. LTV must be supported by independent professional valuation and adjusted for location and condition factors. Higher LTV indicates greater credit risk.

name: Order Independent Professional Property Valuation
description: Required action to obtain independent professional valuation from a qualified surveyor as part of property value assessment process. This valuation forms the basis for LTV calculation and risk assessment in mortgage lending decisions.

name: Compare Property to Comparable Market Data
description: Required action to benchmark the subject property against comparable properties in the market to validate valuation. This comparative analysis supports the independent professional valuation and informs location and condition adjustments.

name: Apply Location and Condition Adjustments to Valuation
description: Required action to adjust the base valuation for identified location and condition risk factors. Adjustments reflect the risk matrix assessment (low/medium/high risk categories) to arrive at a final valuation supporting LTV determination.

name: Confirm Valuation Supports LTV Ratio
description: Required action to validate that the final adjusted property valuation is sufficient to support the proposed loan-to-value ratio. If valuation is insufficient, triggers renegotiation, additional deposit requirement, or borrower shortfall contribution.

name: Credit Risk
description: Credit risk assessment component weighted at 40% in the composite risk scoring framework. Scored at 82 out of 100, contributing 32.8 points to the overall risk evaluation.

name: Income Stability Risk
description: Income stability assessment component weighted at 25% in the composite risk scoring framework. Scored at 85 out of 100, contributing 21.3 points to the overall risk evaluation.

name: Debt-to-Income Risk
description: Debt-to-income ratio assessment component weighted at 20% in the composite risk scoring framework. Scored at 75 out of 100, contributing 15.0 points to the overall risk evaluation.

name: LTV Ratio Risk
description: Loan-to-value ratio assessment component weighted at 15% in the composite risk scoring framework. Scored at 80 out of 100, contributing 12.0 points to the overall risk evaluation.

name: Composite Risk Score
description: Comprehensive composite risk score calculated across four weighted components (Credit Score, Income Stability, Debt-to-Income, and LTV Ratio). The total score of 81.1 out of 100 falls within the 'Good' rating band (75–84), triggering standard approval with manager sign-off.

name: Credit Score Threshold
description: Credit score component of the composite risk assessment, weighted at 40% and scored at 82 out of 100.

name: Income Stability Threshold
description: Income stability component of the composite risk assessment, weighted at 25% and scored at 85 out of 100.

name: Debt-to-Income Ratio Threshold
description: Debt-to-income ratio component of the composite risk assessment, weighted at 20% and scored at 75 out of 100.

name: LTV Ratio Threshold
description: Loan-to-value ratio component of the composite risk assessment, weighted at 15% and scored at 80 out of 100.

name: Risk Score Approval Decision Framework
description: Governance framework establishing approval authority and decision thresholds based on composite risk score bands. Scores of 85–100 receive auto-approval with delegated authority; 75–84 require standard manager sign-off; 65–74 require enhanced risk manager review; 55–64 require senior lending head review; and scores below 55 result in decline.

name: Credit Score Risk
description: Credit score assessment used as a primary underwriting criterion in the lending decision matrix. Scores range from <60 (very high risk, automatic decline) to 90+ (strong candidate for approval). Score thresholds directly determine approval, conditional, or decline outcomes.
context: Credit Score | Income DTI | LTV | Decision

name: Debt-to-Income Ratio Risk
description: Applicant income-to-debt ratio used as a secondary underwriting criterion. DTI thresholds range from <35% (favorable) to >45% (elevated risk). Combined with credit score and LTV, DTI determines lending decision outcome.

name: Loan-to-Value Ratio Risk
description: Loan-to-value ratio threshold used in the underwriting decision matrix. LTV ranges from <75% (lower risk) to >90% (higher risk). LTV combined with credit score and DTI determines approval, conditional, or decline decisions.

name: Default Risk
description: Default risk assessment applied to applicants with credit scores 60–69 (high default risk) or <60 (very high risk), resulting in automatic decline regardless of DTI or LTV. This is the primary risk trigger for lending rejection.

name: Credit Score Threshold
description: Credit score appetite thresholds embedded in the underwriting decision matrix. Scores of 90+ represent strong candidates; 80–89 standard; 70–79 conditional; 60–69 high risk; <60 very high risk with automatic decline.
context: Credit Score | Income DTI | LTV | Decision

name: Debt-to-Income Ratio Threshold
description: DTI appetite thresholds in the underwriting matrix. Favorable DTI is <35%; acceptable is 35–45%; DTI >45% combined with lower credit scores triggers conditional or decline decisions.

name: Loan-to-Value Ratio Threshold
description: LTV appetite thresholds in the underwriting matrix. LTV <80% is favorable; <85% acceptable; <90% standard; >75% combined with lower credit scores triggers conditional review or decline.

name: Underwriting Decision Matrix Approval Framework
description: Formal underwriting decision framework establishing three outcomes (APPROVE, CONDITIONAL, DECLINE) based on credit score, DTI, and LTV combinations. The matrix defines automatic approval for strong candidates (90+ credit score, <35% DTI, <80% LTV) and automatic decline for very high-risk applicants (<60 credit score).
context: Use This Matrix to Make Lending Decisions

name: Conditional Approval Framework
description: A formal approval decision framework that grants conditional approval to borrower applications contingent upon satisfaction of specified conditions. The framework establishes common condition categories including financial documentation, property-related requirements, additional funds, debt reduction, and insurance evidence, with defined management procedures for tracking and release.
context: "Conditional Approval" means: Approved IF conditions are met
Common Conditions: 1. Financial Documentation 2. Property-Related 3. Additional Funds 4. Debt Reduction 5. Insurance
Release funds only after all conditions met

name: Borrower Communication of Approval Conditions
description: Action item requiring the bank to communicate all approval conditions to the borrower as part of the conditional approval process. This is a mandatory step in the condition management workflow.

name: Condition Satisfaction Deadline Setting
description: Action item to establish and communicate a deadline for borrower satisfaction of all approval conditions. The standard deadline is typically 10 days from approval notification.
context: Set deadline for condition satisfaction (typically 10 days)

name: Condition Tracking in System
description: Action item requiring the bank to maintain systematic tracking of all conditions attached to conditional approvals and their satisfaction status throughout the approval lifecycle.

name: Funds Release Upon Condition Satisfaction
aliases: Release funds only after all conditions met
description: Action item establishing the control that funds must only be released to the borrower after all conditions attached to the conditional approval have been fully satisfied and verified.
context: Release funds only after all conditions met

name: Condition Satisfaction Documentation
description: Action item requiring the bank to formally document evidence of condition satisfaction for each conditional approval, creating an audit trail of compliance with approval conditions.

name: Credit Score Risk
description: Risk associated with borrower creditworthiness as measured by credit score. Mandatory decline threshold is <60 indicating very high default risk, with discretionary decline range of 60–69 requiring exceptional credentials for approval.
context: Credit History: Recent late payment on [account]

name: Debt-to-Income Ratio Risk
description: Risk that borrower debt obligations exceed acceptable levels relative to income. Mandatory decline threshold is DTI >45% indicating unaffordable debt burden.
context: Debt Obligations: [Total monthly debt] exceeds [acceptable level]

name: Loan-to-Value Ratio Risk
description: Risk arising from insufficient equity cushion in the property. Mandatory decline threshold is LTV >95% indicating no equity buffer against property value decline.

name: Fraud and Misrepresentation Risk
description: Risk of applicant fraud or material misrepresentation in mortgage application. Mandatory decline trigger when fraud or misrepresentation is detected.

name: Criminal History Risk
description: Risk associated with adverse criminal history of applicant. Mandatory decline trigger when adverse criminal history is present.

name: Bankruptcy Risk
description: Risk arising from recent bankruptcy filing by applicant. Mandatory decline threshold is bankruptcy within 2 years of application.

name: Employment Stability Risk
description: Risk that borrower employment is unstable or insufficient tenure. Discretionary decline trigger when employment is <1 year in unstable field or self-employed <2 years.

name: Property Market Risk
description: Risk that property value may decline due to market conditions. Discretionary decline trigger when property is located in high-risk declining market.

name: Qualifying Income Risk
description: Risk that borrower income is insufficient to qualify for requested loan amount. Referenced in decline letter as key factor when actual income falls below required threshold.
context: Insufficient qualifying income based on your current employment

name: Mortgage Product
description: Mortgage lending product subject to application review and decline criteria. Application includes assessment of borrower creditworthiness, income, debt obligations, and property valuation.
context: We have reviewed your mortgage application dated [date] for the property at [address]

name: Mortgage Applicant
description: Individual applying for mortgage product from FirstUK Bank. Subject to mandatory and discretionary decline criteria based on credit, income, debt, employment, and property factors.
context: We have reviewed your mortgage application dated [date]

name: Mortgage Application Decline Decision
description: Formal lending decision to decline mortgage application based on assessment against mandatory and discretionary decline criteria. Decision communicated to borrower via decline letter with reasons and next steps.
context: Reason: [e.g., "Insufficient qualifying income based on your current employment"]

name: Borrower Credit Issue Resolution
description: Recommended action for declined applicant to resolve outstanding credit issues prior to reapplication. Specific issues identified in decline letter.
context: We recommend: 1. Increase down payment to reduce loan amount 2. Resolve outstanding credit issues 3. Reapply in [months/years] when [condition] is satisfied

name: Borrower Down Payment Increase
description: Recommended action for declined applicant to increase down payment to reduce loan amount and improve LTV ratio for future reapplication.
context: Increase down payment to reduce loan amount

name: Mortgage Application Reapplication
description: Recommended action for declined applicant to reapply for mortgage after specified time period when identified conditions are satisfied.

name: Mortgage Application Credit Report Review
description: Credit report review and verification process conducted as part of mortgage application assessment. Applicant has right to receive copy of credit report and dispute errors.
context: You have the right to receive a copy of your credit report and dispute any errors

name: FCA Complaint Process
description: FCA complaint process referenced in decline letter as avenue for applicant to dispute credit report errors or application decision. Contact information provided.

name: Final Walkthrough by Borrower and Appraiser Pre-Disbursement
description: A pre-disbursement control requiring final walkthrough by borrower and appraiser to confirm no major changes have occurred to the property since initial appraisal. This is a procedural checkpoint documented in the disbursement checklist.
context: Final walkthrough by borrower and appraiser (no major changes)

name: Final Employment Verification Pre-Disbursement
description: A pre-disbursement control requiring final verification of borrower employment via phone call 1–2 days before closing to confirm continued employment status and income stability.
context: Final verification of employment (phone call 1–2 days before closing)

name: Final Credit Check Pre-Disbursement
description: A pre-disbursement control requiring final credit check to confirm no new derogatory marks or new debt have been incurred by the borrower since initial underwriting.
context: Final credit check (no new derogatory marks, new debt)

name: Title Search Clear Title Confirmation Pre-Disbursement
description: A pre-disbursement control requiring title search confirmation that the property has clear title with no liens or claims that would impair the lender's security interest.
context: Title search confirms clear title (no liens, claims)

name: Insurance Policy Obtained and Paid Pre-Disbursement
description: A pre-disbursement control requiring confirmation that the borrower has obtained and paid for required insurance policy coverage on the mortgaged property.

name: All Conditions Satisfied Pre-Disbursement
description: A pre-disbursement control requiring verification that all loan conditions imposed during underwriting have been satisfied by the borrower before funds are released.

name: Closing Disclosure Reviewed and Signed Pre-Disbursement
description: A pre-disbursement control requiring that the Closing Disclosure has been reviewed by the borrower and signed, confirming understanding of final loan terms and costs.

name: Mortgage
description: A mortgage lending product subject to post-approval monitoring controls including monthly payment processing, annual statement verification, ongoing credit monitoring with annual re-scoring, property valuation every 3 years, and default early warning triggers on missed payments.

name: Credit Risk
description: Credit risk on mortgage portfolios managed through ongoing credit monitoring with annual re-scoring and default early warning systems triggered by missed payments.
context: Default early warning (missed payment triggers action)

name: Property Value Risk
description: Risk associated with fluctuations in property values securing mortgage loans, monitored through valuations conducted every 3 years.

name: Credit Re-scoring Frequency
description: Key risk indicator measuring the frequency of credit re-scoring on mortgage accounts to detect deterioration in borrower creditworthiness.

name: Property Valuation Cycle
description: Key risk indicator defining the frequency of property valuations to monitor collateral adequacy and loan-to-value ratios.

name: Missed Payment Default Trigger
description: Key risk indicator and early warning system that flags mortgage accounts upon missed payment to initiate default management procedures.
context: Default early warning (missed payment triggers action)

name: Mortgage Default Risk
description: Risk that a borrower fails to make scheduled mortgage payments, triggering a cascade of mitigation procedures from late notice through foreclosure. The bank faces potential loss if property sale proceeds fall below the remaining loan balance.
context: If Sale Price < Loan Balance: FirstUK Bank absorbs loss

name: Property Value Decline Risk
description: Risk that the mortgaged property depreciates in value, reducing collateral coverage and increasing loss exposure in default scenarios. The document illustrates this with a property decline from £400,000 to £350,000.
context: If Sale Price < Loan Balance: FirstUK Bank absorbs loss

name: Foreclosure Loss Risk
description: Risk of financial loss to the bank when foreclosure proceeds do not fully recover the outstanding loan balance after deducting realtor fees, legal costs, and property taxes.

name: Late Payment Notice Issuance
description: Courtesy notification sent to borrower 15 days after missed payment to alert them of delinquency and provide opportunity to cure.
context: Day 15: Late notice sent (15-day courtesy letter)

name: First Formal Demand for Payment
description: Formal notice issued 30 days after missed payment demanding immediate payment of outstanding amount.
context: Day 30: First formal notice (demand for payment)

name: Second Formal Notice with Right to Cure
description: Second formal notice issued 60 days after missed payment, providing borrower with final opportunity to cure default before cascade proceedings are initiated.
context: Day 60: Second formal notice (right to cure period)

name: Default Declaration and Cascade Proceedings Initiation
description: Formal declaration of default issued 90 days after missed payment, triggering cascade proceedings toward foreclosure if mitigation options are not exercised.

name: Foreclosure and Property Sale Initiation
description: Foreclosure and sale process begins 120+ days after missed payment if default remains unresolved and no mitigation option has been accepted.

name: Payment Plan Offer to Borrower
description: Mitigation option offered to borrower in default, allowing missed payments to be extended over time rather than demanded immediately.
context: Payment Plan — Extend missed payments over time

name: Loan Modification Offer to Borrower
description: Mitigation option offered to borrower in default, allowing modification of loan terms such as extension of maturity or reduction of interest rate.
context: Loan Modification — Change terms (extend, reduce rate)

name: Forbearance Offer to Borrower
description: Mitigation option offered to borrower in default, allowing temporary reduction or suspension of payments.

name: Short Sale Option Offer to Borrower
description: Mitigation option offered to borrower in default, allowing sale of property at a price below the owed amount to avoid foreclosure.
context: Short Sale — Sell property below owed amount

name: Deed in Lieu of Foreclosure Offer to Borrower
description: Mitigation option offered to borrower in default, allowing transfer of property back to the bank instead of proceeding with foreclosure.
context: Deed in Lieu — Transfer property back to bank instead of foreclosure

name: Foreclosure Sale Price
description: The projected sale price of the mortgaged property in a foreclosure scenario, used to calculate net proceeds and potential loss to the bank.

name: Realtor Fees on Foreclosure Sale
description: Realtor fees charged on the foreclosure sale, calculated at 6% of sale price and deducted from gross proceeds.

name: Legal and Court Costs on Foreclosure
description: Legal and court costs incurred in the foreclosure process, deducted from gross sale proceeds.

name: Property Taxes and HOA Charges on Foreclosure
description: Property taxes and homeowners association charges incurred during foreclosure, deducted from gross sale proceeds.

name: Net Proceeds from Foreclosure Sale
description: The net amount recovered from foreclosure sale after deducting realtor fees, legal costs, and property taxes.

name: Outstanding Loan Balance at Foreclosure
description: The remaining principal balance owed by the borrower at the time of foreclosure, used to calculate potential loss to the bank.

name: Borrower Equity in Foreclosure Scenario
description: The borrower's equity position calculated as the difference between net sale proceeds and outstanding loan balance.

name: Bank Loss on Foreclosure
description: The loss absorbed by FirstUK Bank when foreclosure sale proceeds fall short of the outstanding loan balance.
context: If Sale Price < Loan Balance: FirstUK Bank absorbs loss

name: Fair Lending Compliance Risk
description: Risk that FirstUK Bank lending decisions may be based on protected characteristics rather than legitimate credit criteria. The bank has documented prohibited factors (race, color, national origin, religion, sex, gender identity, age, marital status, disability) and approved factors (credit score, payment history, income, employment stability, debt obligations, property value, loan-to-value ratio, down payment amount) to mitigate this risk.
context: FirstUK Bank Does NOT Consider: Race, color, national origin, Religion, Sex, gender identity, Age (except as required by law), Marital status, Disability (must accommodate)
FirstUK Bank DOES Consider: Credit score, payment history, Income and employment stability, Debt obligations, Property value and location, Loan-to-value ratio, Down payment amount
Keep records demonstrating decisions based on credit criteria, not protected characteristics.

name: Fair Lending Documentation Maintenance
description: Ongoing requirement for FirstUK Bank to maintain records that demonstrate all lending decisions are based on approved credit criteria rather than protected characteristics. This is a continuous compliance obligation to support fair lending audit and regulatory review.
context: Keep records demonstrating decisions based on credit criteria, not protected characteristics.

name: Overlooking Recent Late Payments in Credit Assessment
description: A common approval error where recent late payments are not weighted appropriately in credit decisions. The finding highlights that recent payment activity (last 24 months) should be weighted more heavily than historical data to accurately assess current borrower risk.
context: Mistake 1: Overlook recent late payments (weight of recent payment history)
Correct: Weight recent activity (last 24 months) more heavily

name: Accepting Stated Income Without Verification
description: A critical control weakness where applicant income is accepted at face value without independent verification. The correct procedure requires verification through tax returns, W2s, or employer letters to validate income claims.
context: Mistake 2: Accept stated income without verification
Correct: Verify income with tax returns, W2s, employer letters

name: Ignoring Debt-to-Income Ratio When Credit Score is Excellent
description: A control deficiency where high debt-to-income ratios are overlooked because the applicant has an excellent credit score. The finding emphasizes that high DTI increases default risk independent of credit score performance.
context: Mistake 3: Ignore DTI when credit score is excellent
Correct: High DTI increases default risk regardless of credit score

name: Approving Maximum LTV Without Strong Credit and Income Profile
description: A risk control gap where maximum loan-to-value approvals are granted without corresponding strength in the applicant's credit and income profile. Higher LTV lending requires stronger underlying credit and income documentation to mitigate increased default risk.
context: Mistake 4: Approve at max LTV without strong credit and income
Correct: Higher LTV requires stronger credit and income profile

name: Waiving Approval Conditions Without Clear Authorization
description: A governance and control weakness where approval conditions are waived without documented authorization. The finding stresses that conditions exist to reduce risk and any waivers must be clearly documented and authorized.
context: Mistake 5: Waive conditions without clear authorization
Correct: Conditions exist to reduce risk; document any waivers

name: Credit Risk in Mortgage Lending
description: The risk that borrowers will default on mortgage obligations. This risk is managed through multiple controls including recent payment history weighting, income verification, debt-to-income assessment, loan-to-value limits, and condition enforcement.
context: High DTI increases default risk regardless of credit score
Higher LTV requires stronger credit and income profile

name: Standard Approval Decision
description: Lending approval authority granted to CSR/Underwriter for applications meeting standard criteria: credit score 75 or above, debt-to-income ratio below 40%, and loan-to-value ratio below 85%. Decision timeline is 2–3 days.

name: Conditional Approval Decision
description: Lending approval authority granted to Manager for applications with minor conditions and good credit profile. Decision timeline is 3–5 days.

name: Enhanced Review Decision
description: Lending decision authority escalated to Risk Manager for applications with fair credit profiles or edge cases requiring deeper analysis. Decision timeline is 5–7 days.

name: Decline Decision
description: Lending application rejection authority held by Risk Manager for applications with weak credit profiles. Decision timeline is 2–3 days.

name: Appeal Decision
description: Final escalation authority held by Head of Lending when a borrower disputes a lending decline. Appeal decision timeline is 10 days.

name: Debt-to-Income Ratio
description: Debt-to-income ratio threshold used in lending approval decisions. Standard approval threshold is below 40%.

name: Loan-to-Value Ratio
description: Loan-to-value ratio threshold used in lending approval decisions. Standard approval threshold is below 85%.

name: Credit Score Threshold
description: Minimum credit score threshold for standard lending approval. Standard approval requires a score of 75 or above.

name: Risk Appetite Statement 2026
description: FirstUK's formal statement of risk tolerance and appetite levels for 2026, establishing the organization's willingness to accept risk across key business areas.

name: Operational Risk Policy
description: FirstUK's documented risk management framework governing the identification, assessment, monitoring, and mitigation of operational risks across the organization.

name: Risk Assessment Template
description: Standardized procedures and template for conducting comprehensive risk assessments across FirstUK's business operations and product lines.

name: Escalation Matrix
description: Formal authority matrix defining approval levels and escalation procedures for governance decisions and risk-related matters within FirstUK.

name: Incident Response Plan
description: FirstUK's documented procedures for detecting, investigating, and responding to fraud, errors, and other operational incidents.

name: Credit Risk Guide Version 1.0
description: Initial version of a credit risk guide document issued by the Head of Risk on 2026-01-15. This foundational guidance document establishes credit risk management principles and procedures for the organization.
context: Version 1.0 | 2026-01-15 | Initial credit risk guide | Head of Risk

name: Risk Department
description: The department responsible for authoring and maintaining the credit risk guide. The Head of Risk is identified as the author of the initial version of this guidance document.
context: Initial credit risk guide | Head of Risk

name: Head of Risk
description: Senior role responsible for risk oversight and governance. Provided formal approval sign-off on the document dated 2026-01-15.

name: Chief Lending Officer
description: Senior executive responsible for lending operations and credit risk. Provided formal approval sign-off on the document dated 2026-01-15.

name: Compliance Officer
description: Senior compliance role responsible for regulatory adherence and governance compliance. Provided formal approval sign-off on the document dated 2026-01-15.

name: Document Approval by Risk, Lending and Compliance Leadership - 2026-01-15
description: Formal multi-stakeholder approval of the document by Head of Risk, Chief Lending Officer, and Compliance Officer on 2026-01-15, indicating executive sign-off and endorsement of the governance framework or policy contained therein.
